audit.whatIsWrong: diff read 'HARD' while diffRating was 4/10, tone was the favoured green, and report[14] called it a 'Favoured matchup' — four fields, three different answers. The mirror (nasus__heimerdinger) already settled this lane as EVEN 5/10.
audit.why: Win rate 51.32% over 228 games is an even lane, and the mirror audit set diff EVEN / diffRating 5/10 from Nasus's side. Leaving HARD here would have the two pages disagree and mirror-fix.js would overwrite it anyway.
audit.corrected: diff HARD -> EVEN, diffRating 4/10 -> 5/10, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said Heimerdinger wins Level 1 and Level 2 and 'Skill' at first item, while the content prose on the very same page says level 1 is his ('you have one turret charge and no grenade') and that first item swings to Nasus.
audit.why: The packet chart is [Nasus, Skill, Heimerdinger, Heimerdinger, Heimerdinger, Nasus, Nasus] and whys[0], whys[1] and whys[5] already read that way. Only the enum rows were stale.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 -> Nasus, 1 -> Skill, 5 -> Nasus in both layers, with ratings and the three phase whys matched to them. Rows 2, 3, 4 and 6 were already correct.

audit.why: Four spikes present and accurate: his Level 1 stacking window, your 4-5 nest peak, his Level 6 R, his 2+ item takeover.
audit.corrected: No change to spikes; phases[5].why reworded so the first-item row credits Fury of the Sands rather than implying Liandry's decides it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d under 'Fight inside his W slow' described spending one of YOUR spells, not Wither. dosFull[2].d under 'Deny his Q stacks' repeated the trade line instead of saying anything about Siphoning Strike.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s — the single number that decides when you may step up. Siphoning Strike carries an auto-attack reset, so the tell is the attack wind-up, not the cast (flagged missing interaction).
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now gives Wither's 15s rank-1 cooldown; dosFull[2].d now names the auto-reset wind-up as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the text warned that flat resistances are the wrong purchase into Fury of the Sands.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands is flagged percentHealth — it batters nearby enemies for a share of health while giving him bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, so stacking raw MR does not scale against it (flagged missing interaction).
audit.corrected: breakdown.late now states percent-HP damage beats flat MR and points at anti-heal plus range instead.
sources: enemyKit R text and percentHealth flag
